title: One owned thing: Tämä on …
focus: Identify one owned thing with Tämä on and the already learned owner endings.

exercises.prompt: Write “This is his car.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Use auto (“car”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nsa identifies his ownership.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Hänen is the personal owner form of hän; it selects -nsa.
auto (“car”) + -nsa = autonsa. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

Correct: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nsa identifies his ownership.
Use Tämä on for one thing, and keep the owner’s possessive ending.

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your car.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address one person. Use auto (“car”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -si identifies your ownership.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Sinun is the personal owner form of sinä; it selects -si.
auto (“car”) + -si = autosi. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -si: use autosi.
Keep the possessive ending -si even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Sinun needs -si; changing the ending changes the owner.
